summary: A scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology, Heisig studied at Divine Word College, Loyola University Chicago, Notre Dame, and Cambridge (PhD 1973). He held long-term research posts at the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture and served as director of Nanzan University (1991–2001).

Ward was a philosopher who studied at Mostyn House School, Fitzwilliam College, and Trinity College, Cambridge (c. 1872–1875). He held a post at the University of Cambridge from around 1897 to 1925 and taught Surendranath Dasgupta.
Working in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy, Whitehill was attested as Professor of Religion at Stephens College in 2000. He also founded the Columbia Zen Center.

A linguist who studied at Lafayette College and Johns Hopkins University (PhD c. 1882), Bright taught at Cornell in 1885 and held the Caroline Donovan Chair of English at Johns Hopkins (1905–1925). His students included Edwin Whitfield Fay and Franklin Edgerton.

A scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology, he studied under numerous teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Patrul Rinpoche. He taught many disciples, including Shechen Gyaltsab and Ngorpa Pönlob Lo Ter Wangpo.

Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, the 3rd Jamgon Kongtrul studied under the 16th Karmapa, Kalu Rinpoche, Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche, and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje. He taught Richard Barron and Jampa Mackenzie Stewart.

A major figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he studied under numerous masters, including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Tekchok Dorje, and the 9th Tai Situpa. He also taught extensively, with students including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa.

Hubbard works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD), where he was supervised by Minoru Kiyota. By 2016, he held a professorship at Smith College.

Panglung specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earning his Geshe Lharamapa at Sera Monastery and his Magister and Promotion at the University of Munich. He served as a researcher at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities from c. 1975 to 2004.
Stewart is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche and the 3rd Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge.

Samten worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, serving as a bibliographer at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 1987). He held multiple posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, including director (2003–2004) and professor (2015).
Rechung was a scholar of Tibetology who served as Deputy Director at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 1982) and editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology from 1980 to 1988.

Tseveen worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Saint Petersburg around 1902 and held a post at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (1932–1937).

A figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied under many masters, including Shechen Gyaltsab, Khenpo Thupten, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He also taught numerous prominent figures, including Namkhai Norbu, Dilgo Khyentse, and Sogyal Rinpoche.

A central figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied under many teachers, including Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Shechen Gyurme Thutob Namgyal. He was also a prominent teacher whose students included Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Jamyang Sherab Chokyi Nangwa studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
An Indologist, Schoterman studied at Utrecht University, where he was taught by Jan Gonda and supervised by Henk Bodewitz for his doctoral thesis (attested 1982).

Active in Buddhist and religious studies, Bays studied under Taizan Maezumi and Shodo Harada. She earned a medical degree from UC San Diego and became a teacher at the Zen Community of Oregon (1985) and abbess of Great Vow Zen Monastery (c. 2002).
Dolensky is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2013).

Houben works in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He held posts at the Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research (1999) and Leiden University (2000–2002), and became Directeur d'études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 2009–2012).
